questions.stem: What happens when an array index is outside its valid range?
options: The compiler always rejects the program
questions.solution: C++ does not perform automatic bounds checking.

questions.stem: Which operator reads data from cin?
questions.solution: The extraction operator >> reads from an input stream.

options: Translates the whole source program before execution
Executes one source statement at a time
questions.solution: A compiler translates the complete source file into object code.

questions.stem: Which values can a bool variable hold?
questions.solution: A bool holds true or false.

questions.stem: Which declaration creates a floating-point variable named price?
questions.solution: float is used for real numbers.

questions.stem: Which statement is most suitable for selecting among several constant cases?
questions.solution: switch selects a case based on a constant expression.

questions.stem: Which data type stores a whole number?
questions.solution: int stores whole numbers; float stores real values.

questions.stem: Which statement immediately exits a loop?
questions.solution: break terminates the nearest loop or switch.

questions.stem: How many times does a while loop execute when its condition is false initially?
questions.solution: while is a pretest loop; a false condition skips the body.

questions.stem: Which term describes a finite sequence of precise steps that solves a problem?
questions.solution: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of unambiguous steps.

questions.stem: This question tests algorithms and programming errors.

parts.answer: An algorithm is a finite sequence of precise steps that solves a problem. Pseudocode is a structured English-like description of an algorithm.
parts.solution: Award 1 mark for each correct definition.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Explain THREE types of programming errors and give one example of each.
parts.answer: Syntax error: missing semicolon. Runtime error: division by zero. Logic error: using < instead of <= in a condition.
parts.solution: Award 0.5 mark for each type and 0.5 mark for a valid example.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A program reads a student's score from 0 to 100 and displays the grade: 80-100 A, 60-79 B, 50-59 C, 40-49 D, below 40 F.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the grade classification.
parts.answer: Start -> read score -> decision score >= 80 -> A; else score >= 60 -> B; else score >= 50 -> C; else score >= 40 -> D; else F -> display grade -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for terminal symbols, input, four/five decisions, each output and correct flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode for the algorithm and convert it into a complete C++ program.
parts.answer: IF score >= 80 THEN grade = A ELSE IF score >= 60 THEN grade = B ... ENDIF; use if/else if in C++ and display grade.
parts.solution: Award marks for correct pseudocode, complete C++ structure, conditions, input and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests type conversion and constants.

parts.text: Explain the difference between implicit and explicit type conversion, and give one C++ example of each.
parts.answer: Implicit conversion is automatic (int to double); explicit conversion uses a cast such as double(total) or static_cast<double>(total).
parts.solution: Award marks for both definitions and valid examples.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a C++ program segment that calculates the average of three integer marks as a double and displays it to two decimal places.
parts.answer: double average = (m1 + m2 + m3) / 3.0; cout << fixed << setprecision(2) << average;
parts.solution: Award marks for floating-point division, fixed/setprecision and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Trace the program and state the output.
parts.solution: The loop adds 1+2+3+4+5. Award marks for the sequence and final output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Rewrite the loop using a while loop. Then explain what changes if the condition is i < 5.
parts.answer: int i = 1; while (i <= 5) { total += i; i++; } With i < 5 the result is 10 because 5 is not added.
parts.solution: Award marks for correct while structure, update and changed result.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A sports club stores sport names and medal counts in parallel arrays.

parts.text: Declare two parallel arrays for five sports and initialise them with suitable values.
parts.solution: Award marks for both declarations, correct sizes and related indices.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment to display each sport with its medals, then calculate the total and average medals.
parts.answer: Loop i=0..4 to display sports[i] and medals[i], accumulate total, average = double(total)/5.
parts.solution: Award marks for paired display, total, average and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A cafe sells three items: coffee RM8.50, tea RM6.00 and juice RM9.50. A 10% discount is given when the subtotal is at least RM50.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 5 for price/subtotal, 4 for discount, 2 for formatting and 1 for completeness.

parts.text: Write a complete C++ program that reads the item code and quantity, calculates the subtotal and discount, and displays a formatted receipt with the item name, quantity, subtotal, discount and amount to pay.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 5 for price/subtotal, 4 for discount, 2 for formatting and 1 for completeness.

questions.stem: A bookstore records up to five books. Each book has a title, price and quantity in stock.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.

parts.text: Define a struct Book. Write a complete C++ program that reads the records, calculates the total inventory value, and displays the title of the most expensive book.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.
